name: Create MNI coordinate-based ROIS and warp to subject space
summary: Creates spherical and planar ROIs from MNI coordinates and warps them to a subject's T1 space with ANTs SyN registration, outputting an ROIs directory.
description: Builds sphere ROIs (x, y, z, radius) and planar ROIs (axis = coordinate) on the MNI152 1 mm template with wma_pyTools, registers the subject T1 to MNI with antsRegistration (rigid, affine and SyN, using the brain masks), and applies the inverse transform with nearest-label interpolation to bring each ROI into subject space. Use it to define coordinate-based ROIs for tractography segmentation. It needs a T1 and a brain mask of the same subject.

inputs.description: Subject T1-weighted image used as the registration target space for the ROIs.
Brain mask of the subject T1, used to restrict the registration.
inputs.requirements: Must be in the same space as the T1.

outputs.description: The requested spherical and planar ROIs, contained within a directory named "rois".

parameters.description:
Any number of sphere requests, with each request delimited by a semicolon (;).

Within each request, the first three (3) numbers correspond to the X, Y, and Z coordinates of the sphere centroid.  The final (fourth) number corresponds to the sphere radius.  Coordinates can be delimited by commas (,) or spaces ( ).

Any number of planar requests, with each request delimited by a semicolon (;).

Within each request, the first value is a letter (x, y, or z) corresponding to the planar slice the ROI should correspond to.  In this way, x will return a sagittal slice, y will return a coronal slice, and z will return a transverse slice.  The value following the equals (=) symbol corresponds to the spatial coordinate that the plane should occur at along the specified axis.

citations.text: Avesani P, et al. The open diffusion data derivatives, brain data upcycling via integrated publishing of derivatives and reproducible open cloud services. Sci Data 6:69 (2019).
